The study included 15 limb amputees, with 10 in the experimental group receiving the active EMOST treatment and 5 in the control group receiving a sham treatment.
The reduction of phantom limb pain by EMOST was statistically significant (p < 0.05).
Most patients reported a marked improvement in their sleep and mood quality, or a reduction in the frequency of phantom pain after the EMOST treatments.
The EMOST device operates with the non-linear, electromagnetic signals of the patient within a defined frequency range of 1 Hz to 1 MHz, with an electromagnetic intensity of 0.1-10 microteslas.

According to the neuromatrix theory, the regular (painless) neurosignature may be responsible for phantom limb sensations, but phantom pain could be due to an anomalous reorganization of the neuromatrix.

There is emerging evidence that sleep can promote brain plasticity, and the paper suggests that one of the major effects of EMOST may be to influence redox processes in cells and tissues, which can modulate the NMDA receptor, a key molecular structure controlling synaptic plasticity and memory functions.

Low-frequency and low-intensity electromagnetic fields have been shown to influence various cell functions and initiate diverse healing processes, such as the delay of fractures, induction of analgesia, acceleration of wound re-epithelialization, inhibition of inflammatory processes, reduction of fatigue, improvement of multiple sclerosis and chronic pulmonary disease.

Many experiments have provided evidence that reactive oxygen species and reactive nitrogen species and their derivatives act as essential signals in intracellular and intercellular communication, and can stimulate Ca2+-related pathways and free radical/redox-regulated processes.
The paper suggests that several effects of EMOST may be explained (or connected) by redox regulation and membrane processes.
The paper presents only preliminary results and further research would be needed to fully understand the mechanisms and long-term effects of EMOST on phantom limb pain and other health outcomes.

The paper suggests that low-frequency and low-intensity electromagnetic fields can potentially provide useful methods for the treatment of various problematic disorders and can play important roles in the public health of 21st century medicine.
